name: Hair gloss / glaze

angle.text: Users apply a gloss or glaze in a salon or at home to get glossy, smooth-looking hair and to adjust tone for a polished finish. The shine is visible right after treatment and fades over time; clinical studies of these products were not found.

summary: Shine glazes for salon-glossy hair; the effect is cosmetic and temporary, and no clinical studies of the products were found.
note: Sources did not describe gloss formulations specifically.
currentQuick:
Hair gloss or glaze treatments are used to make hair look shinier and smoother.
Reference material describes how conditioners and colorants affect shine, but no clinical studies of gloss products were found.
How it works: Treatments coat the hair or smooth the cuticle so light reflects more evenly. Laboratory work shows luster depends on hair structure and pigmentation [2].
Risks and caveats: Related color products may cause irritation or allergic reactions [1]; effects wash out over time.
deepLead:
A hair gloss or glaze is a shine-boosting treatment used in salons and at home to make hair look glossier and smoother. Encyclopedia coverage of hair coloring does not describe glosses or glazes specifically, though it describes toners that adjust undertones and semi- and demi-permanent colorants that coat or sit beneath the cuticle .
Shine relates to how light scatters from the hair surface. Laboratory research has examined hair luster and how treatments change it, but no clinical studies of gloss or glaze products were found .

name: Hair tape-in / clip-in extensions

angle.text: Users add tape-in or clip-in wefts to get instant length and volume without waiting for hair to grow. The change is visible as soon as they are fitted, and clip-ins can be taken out daily; research on the products' looks effect is not a focus of the literature.

summary: Add-on hair wefts that attach by adhesive tape or clips for instant volume and length; the main documented risk is tension and adhesive damage to natural hair.
note: Prolonged tension or adhesive use is linked to traction alopecia and dermatitis.
currentQuick:
Tape-in and clip-in extensions are strands or wefts of human or synthetic hair that are attached to a person's own hair to add length or thickness. Clip-ins are fastened and removed by the wearer with small clips, while tape-ins are bonded to the natural hair with adhesive strips.
In appearance communities they are discussed as a way to add visible volume without a procedure, mostly by people with thin or short hair. No clinical trials were found that test their appearance benefit.
How it works: Hair wefts are attached to the natural hair (not the scalp) by clips or adhesive tape, adding visible density and length. They do not affect the underlying hair or follicles.
Risks and caveats: Dermatology references describe traction alopecia (hair loss at the hairline or around the ears) from prolonged tension, and adhesives can cause dermatitis or headaches. Wikipedia notes patch testing is advised before using bonding products.
deepLead:
Hair extensions, also called weaves or hair integrations, add length or volume to natural hair by clipping, gluing or sewing in human or synthetic hair. Tape-in and clip-in are two of the attachment methods listed for them, alongside micro or nano rings, fusion, weaving and wigs.
In looksmaxxing and grooming discussions, extensions are mentioned as a non-surgical way to add apparent hair density. No clinical studies were found that evaluate extensions for appearance, and most published description concerns hair-care and hair-loss risks rather than aesthetic outcomes.

name: Testosterone / TRT for beard

angle.text: Forum posters use testosterone or TRT hoping to fill in a patchy beard, since androgens and DHT drive facial hair development at puberty. Beard growth is a recognised virilizing effect of testosterone in medical use, though it has not been studied as a standalone cosmetic goal.

summary: Using testosterone replacement or similar androgens to push facial hair growth; androgens do drive beard growth, but the practice carries well-documented hormonal and legal risks.
note: Controlled substance in many countries; suppresses natural testosterone and sperm production.
currentQuick:
Beard growth begins at puberty and is driven by androgens, mainly dihydrotestosterone (DHT) made from testosterone. Some people in looksmaxxing communities therefore discuss testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) as a route to a fuller beard.
Testosterone is a prescription medication used chiefly for hypogonadism and gender-affirming care. It is not approved for cosmetic beard growth, and no trials were found that test it for that purpose in men with normal levels.
How it works: Testosterone is converted in hair follicles to DHT, which stimulates facial hair follicles; beard growth rate is also described as largely genetic.
Risks and caveats: Documented effects of exogenous testosterone include acne, fluid retention, gynecomastia, raised hematocrit, suppressed sperm production, worsened sleep apnea and, for scalp hair, possible androgenetic hair loss. It is a controlled substance in many jurisdictions (Schedule III in the US) and contraindicated in pregnancy.
deepLead:
Testosterone is an androgen hormone used as a medication, principally for male hypogonadism, and also in gender-affirming therapy. Its virilizing effects include growth of facial and body hair. Beard development begins at puberty and is stimulated by dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which is made from testosterone.
In looksmaxxing discussions, testosterone replacement therapy is sometimes raised as a way to increase beard density. Reference sources describe the hormonal mechanism but report that the rate of beard growth is largely genetic. The same sources document adverse effects and legal controls on testosterone.

name: Beard vitamins (zinc, B-complex, D)

angle.text: Beard-growth stacks combine zinc, B vitamins such as biotin, and vitamin D, with users aiming for a thicker, healthier beard. Deficiencies in some of these nutrients are linked to thin hair, but trials of extra vitamins for beard growth specifically were not found.

summary: Multivitamin-style stacks of zinc, B vitamins and vitamin D aimed at beard growth; deficiencies can affect hair, but no trials show extra vitamins thicken a beard.
note: Biotin can interfere with some lab tests; high vitamin D intake can be toxic.
currentQuick:
Some beard-growth routines include over-the-counter zinc, B-complex (often biotin) and vitamin D, on the idea that nutrient shortfalls limit facial hair.
Reference sources link deficiencies of some of these nutrients to hair thinning, but no clinical trials were found testing them for beard growth in people who are not deficient.
How it works: Zinc, biotin and other B vitamins are involved in skin and hair biology, and deficiency states are associated with hair changes. Whether supplementing beyond adequate intake changes beard growth has not been studied.
Risks and caveats: Biotin at 5 mg/day or more can distort thyroid and vitamin D lab results. Vitamin D toxicity, with high blood calcium, can occur at very high doses. Supplements in the US are not approved for effectiveness before sale.
deepLead:
Beard-growth stacks sold or discussed online often combine zinc, B-complex vitamins (frequently biotin) and vitamin D. Deficiencies of some of these nutrients are associated with hair changes: zinc deficiency with thin, sparse hair, and biotin deficiency, which is rare, with hair thinning.
Reference sources report that there are no randomized controlled trials proving biotin supplementation helps healthy people's hair, and general hair-loss references state that dietary supplements are not typically recommended. No studies found address these vitamins specifically for beard growth.

name: Tretinoin for beard

angle.text: Some beard routines add prescription tretinoin to minoxidil on the theory that it boosts absorption and results. This is discussed online as an off-label combination; beard-specific evidence for the tretinoin addition is lacking.

summary: Adding prescription tretinoin to minoxidil to boost beard growth; the combination is discussed online but beard-specific evidence is lacking.
note: Prescription retinoid; irritation and sun sensitivity are common, and it is harmful in pregnancy.
currentQuick:
Tretinoin is a prescription vitamin A derivative used on skin for acne and photoaging. In beard-growth forums it is sometimes mixed or layered with minoxidil on the theory that it improves absorption.
A general reference notes the evidence for tretinoin boosting minoxidil in hair loss is weak and contradictory, and no beard studies were found.
How it works: Tretinoin binds retinoic acid receptors and normalizes follicle keratinization; the proposed minoxidil link is increased conversion of minoxidil to its active sulfate form.
Risks and caveats: Topical use commonly causes redness, peeling, irritation and sun sensitivity; oral tretinoin is contraindicated in pregnancy. It is prescription-only in the US, UK and EU.
deepLead:
Tretinoin (all-trans retinoic acid) is a retinoid prescribed mainly for acne, and for photoaging; the oral form treats acute promyelocytic leukemia. In some beard-growth routines it is combined with minoxidil, which is approved for scalp hair loss and used off-label for beard growth.
Wikipedia reports tretinoin has been studied with minoxidil for hair loss, partly for its possible ability to increase minoxidil sulfate production, and describes the evidence as weak and contradictory. No studies found on tretinoin for beard growth.

name: Beard growth serum / Kirkland minox foam

angle.text: Users apply over-the-counter 5% minoxidil foam, often a store-brand version, to the beard to fill patchy areas. It is an off-label use of a scalp hair-loss product; published trials on beard growth exist, including in transgender men and in beard enhancement.

summary: Over-the-counter 5% minoxidil foam, often a store-brand like Kirkland, used off-label on the beard; the only active ingredient with trial evidence for beard growth.
note: Off-label for beard use; effects reportedly reverse when stopped; beard "serums" vary in ingredients.
currentQuick:
Minoxidil is an over-the-counter topical sold for scalp hair loss, and 5% foam products, including store brands, are widely discussed for beard growth. Commercial beard "serums" are a separate and varied category.
Small randomized trials of minoxidil lotion for beard enhancement exist, and Wikipedia lists beard growth as an off-label use.
How it works: Minoxidil is a prodrug converted in follicles to minoxidil sulfate, an ATP-sensitive potassium channel opener; proposed hair effects include increased blood flow and growth-factor induction.
Risks and caveats: Topical use can cause itching, irritation and dandruff; hypertrichosis (unwanted hair growth) is described, and benefits reverse when use stops.
deepLead:
Minoxidil topical foam and solution are sold over the counter in the US for androgenetic alopecia, with 5% foam approved in 2006 and generics following in 2017. Beard growth is described as an off-label use, and trials have been published in transgender men and in beard enhancement generally.
Commercial beard growth serums are marketed under many brand names; the contents differ by product, and no studies found address them as a class.

name: Beard growth supplements (Beardalicious, etc.)

angle.text: Branded beard pills, usually vitamin and herbal blends, are promoted to users who want fuller facial hair. The appearance benefit is a marketing claim; published trials of these products were not found.

summary: Branded pills marketed for beard growth, usually vitamin and herbal blends; no published trials were found for any of them.
note: US supplements are not approved for effectiveness before sale; some contain unlisted ingredients.
currentQuick:
Beard growth pills are commercially sold supplements, typically blends of vitamins such as biotin and herbal extracts, promoted with claims about thicker facial hair.
No clinical studies were found for these branded products.
How it works: Marketing generally points to individual ingredients such as biotin; products vary and no mechanism for beard growth has been demonstrated.
Risks and caveats: In the US, supplements may be sold without premarket approval, and some analyses cited by Wikipedia found mislabeling or undeclared drugs in certain categories. Biotin can interfere with lab tests.
deepLead:
Beard growth supplements are branded oral products, often vitamin or herbal blends, promoted for facial hair. In the US they are regulated as dietary supplements, which can carry structure/function claims with an FDA disclaimer but are not required to be approved before sale.
Reference sources report no randomized trials showing biotin helps hair in healthy people, and that dietary supplements are generally not recommended for hair loss. No studies found address specific branded beard supplements.

name: Shave to thicken myth

chain: Hair seems thicker or more even
angle.text: Men with patchy beards shave the area in the belief that hair returns thicker, darker or faster to even things out. Published sources report that shaving does not change the hair's growth, so this remains a belief rather than a studied effect.

summary: The idea that shaving makes hair grow back thicker; published sources report it does not.
note: Perceived thickness is attributed to blunt tips and age, not follicle change.
currentQuick:
Some people believe shaving makes hair return thicker, darker or faster, and apply this to patchy beards.
Wikipedia reports that shaving does not change terminal hair thickness, coarseness or darkness.
How it works: Proponents propose that cutting stimulates follicles. Sources attribute the impression to blunt-cut tips, stiffness of short hair, sun-lightened longer hair and age-related changes.
Risks and caveats: No notable harms are specific to the belief; ordinary shaving irritation can occur.
deepLead:
The belief that shaving makes facial or body hair grow back thicker, darker or faster is a long-circulating grooming idea that is also discussed in beard-growth circles, where some men shave to try to even out patchy growth.
Wikipedia's article on shaving states that shaving does not cause terminal hair to grow back thicker, coarser or darker, and offers explanations for why the impression arises. The idea is classed here as a looksmaxxing belief with no published trial supporting it.

name: Growing it out 12 weeks

angle.text: Beard growers leave facial hair untrimmed for about three months before deciding whether it fills in well enough to keep. The aim is a fuller, better-shaped beard; the 12-week figure is a community rule of thumb with no research behind it.

summary: A three-month no-trim patience rule for beards; the 12-week figure itself has no research behind it.
currentQuick:
Some beard-growers leave facial hair untrimmed for about 12 weeks before judging it.
The specific timeframe is a community convention; no studies test it.
How it works: The idea is that growth and filling-in need time. Biology sources describe beard growth as DHT-driven and partly genetic.
Risks and caveats: No specific harms are documented; the approach does not change genetic limits on growth.
deepLead:
"Growing it out 12 weeks" is a patience protocol discussed in beard-growing communities: leaving facial hair untrimmed for roughly three months before judging its density and pattern.
Beard growth begins at puberty and is linked to dihydrotestosterone, with growth rate partly genetic, according to Wikipedia. No published study was found that tests a 12-week benchmark specifically.

name: Beard fillers / fibers / pencils

angle.text: Users apply beard pencils and fibers to fill sparse or patchy areas for an instantly denser look. The effect is visible immediately and lasts until washed off, without changing hair growth.

summary: Cosmetic pencils and fibers that fake beard density; temporary and visual only.
currentQuick:
These are cosmetic products that darken or thicken the look of sparse beard areas.
They are temporary and do not affect hair growth.
How it works: They add pigment or fiber bulk to skin and hair so gaps appear covered.
Risks and caveats: No published safety data were found; skin reactions are possible with any cosmetic, and product labels give guidance.
deepLead:
Beard fillers, fibers and pencils are cosmetic products intended to visually fill sparse or patchy areas of facial hair, giving a denser look without changing hair growth.
Users in grooming communities describe them as a temporary fix. Published research on these specific products was not found, and sources reviewed give no data on price, safety or effectiveness.

name: Beard concealer powder

angle.text: Users dust tinted powder over thin spots to hide patches and give an even beard color. The coverage is visible straight away and temporary.

summary: Tinted powder to hide beard patches; cosmetic and temporary.
currentQuick:
A cosmetic powder applied to cover thin or patchy beard areas.
The effect is temporary and visual only.
How it works: The powder adds colour to skin and hair to reduce contrast between bare and covered areas.
Risks and caveats: No safety data were found; ordinary cosmetic skin reactions are possible.
deepLead:
Beard concealer powder is a cosmetic product used to cover patches or thin areas in a beard by tinting skin or hair.
No published studies on these products were found, and detailed community or product material was unavailable for this entry.

name: Chinstrap / goatee / designer stubble styling

chain: Altered face shape and chin look
angle.text: Men with patchy beards use chinstrap, goatee or designer-stubble cuts to look groomed and to alter perceived face shape, for example adding chin projection and contrast. The visible result depends on growth pattern and jaw, and is discussed mainly through forum anecdote.

summary: Limited beard styles used to work around patchiness; results vary by growth pattern and jaw.
currentQuick:
Styling facial hair into a goatee, chinstrap or short stubble is used to deal with patchy growth or alter face shape.
Forum users report mixed results that depend on growth pattern and facial structure.
How it works: Hair is kept only in selected zones to add contrast or frame the mouth and chin.
Risks and caveats: No medical risks are documented; outcomes are subjective.
deepLead:
Chinstrap, goatee and designer-stubble styling refers to shaping facial hair into limited patterns to work around patchy growth or to alter perceived face shape. Wikipedia defines a goatee as chin hair without cheek hair, a term that broadened by the 1990s to cover chin styles generally.
Users on looksmax.org discuss stubble and goatees as ways to add contrast to the lower face, and also report that results depend on growth pattern and jaw structure. No clinical studies were found on these styles.

name: Beard brush / comb

angle.text: Users brush or comb the beard to detangle, spread product and shape it, with some describing it as training hair to lie in one direction. The tidier look is immediate; there is no evidence it changes growth.

summary: Brush or comb for tidying and shaping a beard; no evidence it changes growth.
currentQuick:
Tools for detangling and shaping facial hair.
Some users say brushing helps train hair direction.
How it works: Bristles or teeth align and spread hairs; no research shows an effect on follicle growth.
Risks and caveats: No notable risks are documented; vigorous use can irritate skin.
deepLead:
Beard brushes and combs are grooming tools used to detangle, shape and distribute product through facial hair. Some beard-growers also describe brushing as "training" the hair to lie in a direction.
Combs date back to prehistoric times, per Wikipedia, though its article does not cover beard combs specifically. No studies of beard brushing for appearance or growth were found.

name: Beard wash / conditioner

chain: Gentle cleansing of beard and skin
angle.text: Users wash and condition the beard with products made for facial hair, often alongside oils and balms, for a softer feel and cleaner look. The grooming benefit is visible and tactile; dedicated clinical studies were not found.

summary: Cleansers and softeners made for facial hair; popular grooming staples with no dedicated clinical studies.
note: No clinical studies of beard-specific washes or conditioners were found.
currentQuick:
Beard wash and conditioner are grooming products sold to clean and soften facial hair and the skin under it. They are usually presented as gentler than ordinary shampoo.
They became more visible as full beards returned to fashion in the 2010s. No clinical studies of these specific products were found.
How it works: Washes are cleansers and conditioners are softening agents, as marketed. Their effects on beard appearance or skin have not been tested in published trials found for this entry.
Risks and caveats: Risks are generally those of any cosmetic product, such as skin irritation or allergy to an ingredient. Medical sources attribute razor bumps mainly to shaving and hair curling back into skin rather than to washing products.
deepLead:
Beard wash and beard conditioner are grooming products marketed for cleaning and softening facial hair and the skin beneath it. They are positioned as alternatives to ordinary shampoo and soap, and are often sold alongside beard oils and balms.
Beard care products have grown in commercial visibility since full beards became fashionable among younger men in the 2010s, a period in which sales of male grooming products rose sharply . Looksmaxxing communities generally treat beard care as part of skin and facial-hair maintenance rather than as a growth intervention.
No published clinical studies of dedicated beard washes or conditioners were found. General dermatology sources discuss beard-area skin problems such as razor bumps mainly in connection with shaving technique and exfoliating treatments rather than washing products .

name: Ingrown hair prevention (salicylic)

chain: Clearer skin on beard and neck
angle.text: Men who shave use topical salicylic acid to reduce razor bumps and ingrown hairs on the beard and neck for smoother skin. It is a common grooming suggestion; direct trial evidence is limited, and shaving habits are often cited as equally important.

summary: Salicylic acid exfoliation for razor bumps: a common grooming suggestion with limited direct trial evidence.
note: Can irritate skin; references describe stronger evidence for beard growth, trimming, glycolic acid and benzoyl peroxide.
currentQuick:
This practice uses topical salicylic acid to exfoliate shaved areas so hairs are less likely to curl back into the skin.
Medical references call it a common remedy and describe salicylic peels as effective for razor bumps, but the cited trials mostly concern glycolic acid and benzoyl peroxide.
How it works: Salicylic acid makes surface skin cells shed more readily, which is said to keep pores from clogging and free trapped hairs.
Risks and caveats: Possible skin and eye irritation. Cosmetic use is described in one review as not posing significant systemic risk, though salicylate toxicity has been documented with large-area high-strength use. The EU sets concentration limits.
deepLead:
Ingrown hair prevention with salicylic acid refers to the use of topical salicylic acid, a keratolytic (skin-shedding) ingredient, to reduce razor bumps and ingrown hairs in shaved areas such as the beard and neck. It is a common suggestion in grooming and skincare discussions.
An ingrown hair occurs when a hair curls back or grows sideways into the skin; it is most common with coarse or curly hair and in shaved or waxed areas . When inflamed it is called pseudofolliculitis barbae (PFB), or razor bumps .
Medical references describe salicylic acid peels as effective for PFB, but the supporting clinical evidence cited in those references is thin; the best-described trials concern glycolic acid and benzoyl peroxide combinations . Salicylic acid is regulated as a cosmetic ingredient in the EU with concentration limits .

name: Sleep and testosterone optimization

angle.text: Men use sleep habits, training and leanness as a drug-free way to protect or raise natural testosterone, hoping for better beard growth and physique. The links between poor sleep and lower testosterone are plausible, with little direct human trial evidence for the appearance outcomes.

summary: Sleep, leanness and training as a drug-free testosterone strategy; plausible links, little direct human trial evidence.
note: Sources reviewed contain no human trials of sleep interventions on testosterone.
currentQuick:
This lifestyle approach tries to raise natural testosterone through sleep, a lean physique, training and diet, often as an alternative to prescription hormones.
Testosterone follows a morning peak and REM sleep is associated with higher night levels, but the sources reviewed contain no human trials of sleep interventions.
How it works: Proposed routes are circadian and sleep-related hormone release, less aromatization of testosterone in fat tissue, and training effects. Reference sources describe the body-fat evidence as mixed.
Risks and caveats: The practices themselves are ordinary lifestyle habits. Concerns raised in sources include assuming low testosterone without testing; diagnosis relies on blood tests, preferably in the morning.
deepLead:
Sleep and testosterone optimization is a lifestyle practice in which men try to raise or protect their natural testosterone through sleep habits, often together with training, leanness and diet. It is popular among people who want to avoid prescription hormone use.
Reference sources note that testosterone follows a daily rhythm, peaking in the morning and falling through the day, and that REM sleep is associated with higher night-time levels . One article reports animal research linking prolonged sleep deprivation to lower testosterone in males .
Observational research links low testosterone to insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome in men . The sources reviewed did not include trials testing sleep interventions on testosterone in men.

name: Lift heavy / low body fat for T

chain: Heavy lifting and low body fat
angle.text: Muscle and looksmaxxing communities suggest heavy resistance training and staying lean to lift natural testosterone, in pursuit of a more muscular look and better beard growth. Acute rises after lifting are reported; long-term effects on baseline levels are less clear.

summary: Heavy lifting plus leanness as a drug-free testosterone strategy; acute rises are reported, long-term effects are less clear.
note: Reference sources describe the body-fat and testosterone evidence as mixed.
currentQuick:
This practice uses heavy resistance training and low body fat to try to raise natural testosterone.
Reference sources report acute testosterone rises after resistance training and a possible increase with weight loss, while describing the evidence on body fat as mixed.
How it works: Resistance training acutely raises testosterone, and less fat tissue means less aromatase converting testosterone to estradiol, as proposed in reference sources.
Risks and caveats: Training itself carries ordinary injury risks. Sources note that endurance training may lower testosterone, and diagnosing low testosterone relies on blood testing.
deepLead:
Lifting heavy and staying lean to raise testosterone is a training-and-body-composition practice in which men use resistance training and low body fat in an attempt to increase natural testosterone levels. It is a common drug-free suggestion in muscle and looksmaxxing discussions.
Reference sources report that resistance training raises testosterone acutely, that endurance training may lower it, and that weight loss may raise it because fat tissue contains aromatase, which converts testosterone to estradiol . The same source also notes that no clear association between body mass index and testosterone has been found, so the evidence on body fat is mixed .
Evidence is limited in the sources reviewed for this entry.

name: Clomiphene / enclomiphene

angle.text: Bodybuilding and looksmaxxing users take clomiphene or enclomiphene off-label to raise their own testosterone without injections, or to restart the axis after steroid cycles. Trials exist in hypogonadal men for testosterone levels, but none address appearance.

summary: A fertility SERM used off-label by men to raise their own testosterone; trial data in hypogonadal men, none for looks.
note: Prescription-only; visual disturbances reported; WADA-prohibited; enclomiphene never approved.
currentQuick:
Clomiphene is an oral fertility drug that men also use off-label to raise their own testosterone. Enclomiphene is its more androgenic isomer.
Trials in men with secondary hypogonadism report testosterone rises. No studies were found on appearance outcomes.
How it works: It blocks estrogen feedback in the brain, increasing LH and FSH signals that drive testicular testosterone production.
Risks and caveats: The label lists ovarian enlargement and flushes in women, and visual symptoms that can occasionally be prolonged. Enclomiphene was refused EU authorization in 2018. Clomiphene is prescription-only and WADA-prohibited.
deepLead:
Clomiphene (clomifene, brand Clomid) is an oral selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) approved for treating ovulatory dysfunction in women . In men it is used off-label to raise the body's own testosterone, and it is discussed in bodybuilding and looksmaxxing communities as a way to do this without testosterone injections or to restart the axis after steroid cycles .
Clomiphene is a mixture of roughly 62 percent enclomiphene and 38 percent zuclomiphene isomers . Enclomiphene, the more antiestrogenic isomer, was developed as a purified drug for men with secondary hypogonadism, but regulatory approval was not obtained and development was discontinued in 2021 .
Trials in hypogonadal men report raised testosterone . Reported adverse effects include visual symptoms, and the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibits clomiphene . No published trial was found testing it for facial or appearance outcomes.

name: hCG

angle.text: Users add prescription hCG to testosterone protocols to keep the testes active and support natural hormone production alongside muscle and beard goals. Its role is established in medicine; effects on looks have not been studied.

summary: An LH-mimicking Rx hormone used with testosterone to keep the testes active; established in medicine, unstudied for looks.
note: Prescription-only; banned in sport; OTC weight-loss products have been called fraudulent by the FDA.
currentQuick:
hCG is a pregnancy hormone that imitates LH. Medically it triggers ovulation and treats some male hypogonadism.
In forums, men on testosterone use it to keep testicles functioning. No studies were found on appearance outcomes.
How it works: It binds the LH receptor, prompting the ovary or testes to produce sex hormones, including testosterone from Leydig cells.
Risks and caveats: Reference warnings include thromboembolism and multiple pregnancy in women, and precocious puberty risk in prepubescent teenagers. Prescription-only in the US and banned in several sports.
deepLead:
Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a hormone made by the placenta that resembles luteinizing hormone (LH) and can trigger ovulation in women and stimulate testosterone production in the testes . Pharmaceutical hCG is prescription-only and is made from the urine of pregnant women or by recombinant DNA .
In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities hCG is discussed mainly by men using testosterone or anabolic steroids, who say it helps maintain testicular size and function during and after cycles . Some posters also discuss it alongside other compounds for facial or bone changes, claims for which no studies were found.
In medicine hCG treats some forms of male hypogonadism, supports fertility treatment, and is used as a tumor marker . The FDA has stated over-the-counter hCG weight-loss products are fraudulent .

name: Castor oil beard

angle.text: Users rub castor oil into the face in the belief it thickens or fills in facial hair; it is also an emollient that leaves hair looking glossy. Growth claims are widespread online, while beard-specific studies were not found.

summary: Castor oil rubbed on the face for fuller facial hair; widely claimed online, with no beard studies behind it.
note: No studies on beard growth; rare contact allergy reported.
currentQuick:
Castor oil is a thick plant oil that some people apply to the jaw and cheeks hoping for denser facial hair. The claim circulates mainly through social media and hair-care forums.
No study has tested it for beard growth. Reference sources say evidence for hair growth in general is weak or indirect, limited to making hair look glossier.
How it works: Proponents say the oil improves follicle circulation or moisture. Beard growth is understood to depend mainly on androgens such as dihydrotestosterone and on genetics, and no mechanism for a topical oil has been shown.
Risks and caveats: Topical castor oil is generally considered low-risk, with rare contact dermatitis reported, especially undiluted. It is an over-the-counter cosmetic product.
deepLead:
Castor oil beard refers to the practice of applying castor oil, a vegetable oil pressed from the seeds of Ricinus communis, to the face in the belief that it thickens or fills in facial hair. Castor oil is about 90 percent ricinoleic acid, and has a long history of medicinal and cosmetic use, mainly as a laxative and an emollient.
Published sources reviewed for this article contain no beard-specific research. A general reference work on castor oil says it is promoted online for hair, lash and brow growth, and that no high-quality studies show it stimulates follicle growth or density. Beard growth is understood to be driven largely by androgens, especially dihydrotestosterone, and to be partly genetic.
